messages:
Annika: Heads up — Mistral-Spark soft launch is T+7. Early traffic tests show APAC/EU tail latencies and token/sec way higher than we modeled. Need quick capacity+network check. Anyone on?
Samir: tagging numbers from the perf run this morning: peak observed tokens/sec ~1.2M global during the replay (10% sample). APAC accounted for ~520k of that.
Liam: confirmed. Replay had hotter sessions from SE-APAC customers — median seq len 1024, heavy streaming. mean tokens/req went up 2.2x vs baseline.
Annika: Can you translate to GPUs hours? We need to know reserved vs burst needs and if Dedicated pools can cover.
Samir: Rough calc: with our current nv24-type instances (measured for this model) we get ~60k tok/s per GPU at target latency SLO. So 520k APAC -> ~8.7 GPUs concurrent peak. Call it 9-10 to be safe. EU ~380k -> ~6.5 => 7 GPUs. NA lower ~300k -> 5 GPUs.
Marco: wait — 60k tok/s per GPU was for 2048k context with beam=1? Which profile did you use Samir?
Samir: micro-bench used beam=1, quantized FP16 runtime, batching tuned for 8x latency windows. If customers enable streaming + small batches, throughput drops ~15-25% depending on session mix. I'm already applying a 20% safety margin in the numbers above.
Yuna: network note: asia-northeast1 has a hard egress cap we hit in the replay (throttled at ~6Gbps per zone). If we scale GPUs in that region, we need extra cross-zone bandwidth or move replicas to asia-south1.
Liam: moving replicas impacts p95 latency for nearby users. If we route APAC to asia-south1, expect +40-55ms p95 delta. Not ideal for interactive flows.
Annika: Operational asks: 1) how many additional reserved GPUs for APAC/EU to buy for launch week? 2) fallback routing plan if asia-northeast1 bandwidth saturates? 3) cost delta estimate for Dedicated vs burst.
Samir: Recommendation: reserve 12 GPUs in APAC (gives headroom for spikes & rolling upgrades), 8 in EU, keep NA burst-on-demand. That maps to ~ (12+8)*24 = 480 GPU-hours/day reserved. Over launch week (7d) ~3.36k GPU-hours.
Marco: cost: on committed pricing that’s ~ $0.85/GPU-hour on our Dedicated pool (internal rate) -> ~ $2.86k/week in committed cost. Burst usage (on-demand) avg rate ~ $1.90/GPU-hour, so extra if we miss reservation.
sre-bot: ALERT POLICY UPDATED — 'mistral-spark-apac-egress' threshold set to 5.5 Gbps per zone by Marco at 1965000058
Yuna: For network fallback: proposal A) enable cross-region proxy to route APAC non-interactive batch to asia-south1; B) keep interactive traffic on north1 but throttle non-critical routes (e.g., embeddings). We can implement B in ~2 hours if config approved.
Liam: Routing policy snippet (canary) I propose:
```
if region == "asia" and observed_egress_zone > 5Gbps:
  route(priority==interactive) -> asia-northeast1
  route(priority==background) -> asia-south1
end
```
Annika: Nice. Can we enforce per-customer tier so free-tier background jobs get moved first?
Marco: yes — per-route metadata exists. Also suggest enabling prefix caching for common system prompts — that will shave ~8-12% token load in steady-state. Ops can push a list of hot prefixes to the cache before launch.
Samir: Updated GPU math with prefix cache impact: assume 10% reduction effective tokens -> APAC peak drops 520k -> ~468k => ~7.8 GPUs => round up to 9. So reservation of 12 still safe.
Yuna: I also measured power/connect slot constraints in APAC DC: one rack has 14 usable GPUs available for quick spin-up; above that we need 48hr notice for power provisioning. We should provision across 2 racks to avoid single-rack risk.
Liam: Can Dedicated autoscaler handle hot rebalancing across racks/zones? We need to confirm eviction/fallback behavior if a rack loses network or power.
Marco: It can, but cross-zone bring-up increases cold-start time ~90s for first token due to kernel warmup. For interactive SLOs we'd prefer keeping warm standby rather than full cold scale.
Annika: Ops decision window: do we reserve 12APAC/8EU now? This will lock some capacity and cost. If yes, Marco and Yuna to submit the reservation ticket.
Samir: Financial fallback calc: Worst-case month if spikes persist (3x baseline) -> we'd spend additional on-demand ~ (extra 20 GPUs * 24 * 30) * $1.90 = ~$27k/month. With reservation it's cheaper.
Marco: I'm in favor of reservation. I'll open a ticket with infra-proc and cc ops-na. Yuna can include the rack placement request.
Yuna: Opening ticket now. ETA to vendor confirmation 26 hours.
Annika: Also: rollouts. We should canary Mistral-Spark with 5% traffic for 6 hours, then 20% overnight, then full. Need autoscale runway for each step.
Liam: Canary policy (example) —
```json
{"canary": [{"percent": 5, "duration": "6h"}, {"percent": 20, "duration": "12h"}, {"percent": 100, "duration": "rollout"}], "fallback": "route-to-quantized-lite"}
```
Annika: Who owns the fallback variant 'quantized-lite'? Ops or Model-onboarding?
Samir: Model-onboarding owns the instance but ops runs the fallback routing. Samir and Dan from onboarding will sync after this thread.
Marco: Quick network mitigation we can do before reservation is confirmed: enable per-connection muxing (reduces egress by ~15%) and set aggressive HTTP/2 windowing. Ops can flip flags via remote-config. That gives us breathing room for 24-36hrs.
Yuna: Done. I flipped muxing on the staging proxy. Will flip prod after smoke test (30m).
Annika: Last: monitoring. Update dashboards to show token/sec per-region, p95 latency, egress per zone, and GPU utilization per rack. Add a 'launch-day' view for oncall.
sre-bot: DASHBOARD CREATED — 'mistral-spark-launch' by Liam at 1965000098
Annika: Great. Thanks everyone. Marco/Yuna — keep me posted once procurement ticket is in and prod muxing is live. I'll coordinate the canary window with growth.
Marco: ticket  #INFRA-3419 created (procurement+rack placement). ETA vendor conf within 26h.
Yuna: Prod muxing scheduled for +40m after staging smoke.
Samir: I'll publish a short runbook (GPU scale-up, network fallback steps, rollback to quantized-lite) in the infra runbooks channel in 45m.
Annika: Perfect. Closing thread unless there are blockers.
Liam: no blockers from SRE.
Annika: thanks :thumbsup:
